questions.text: An array of n numbers is given, where n is an even number. The maximum as well as the minimum of these n numbers needs to be determined. Which of the following is TRUE about the number of comparisons needed?
questions.solution: Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: At least 2n - c comparisons, for some constant c, are needed.
At least 2 nlog n comparisons are needed.

questions.text:
Given two arrays of numbers [latex]a_{1},...,a_{n}[/latex] and [latex]b_{1},...,b_{n}[/latex] where each number is 0 or 1,
the fastest algorithm to find the largest span(i,j) such that [latex]a_{i}+a_{i+1}+...+a_{j}=b_{i}+b_{i+1}+.....+b_{j}[/latex] , or report that there is no such span,
questions.solution: Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Takes [latex]O(3^{n})[/latex] and [latex]\Omega (2^{n})[/latex] time if hashing is permitted
Takes [latex]O(n^{3})[/latex] and [latex]\Omega (n^{2.5})[/latex] time in the key comparison model
Takes [latex]O(\sqrt{n})[/latex] time only if the sum of the 2n elements is an even number

questions.text:
An element in an array X is called a leader if it is grater than all elements to the
right of it in X. The best algorithm to find all leaders in an array.
questions.solution: Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Solves it in linear time using a left to right pass of the array
Solves in linear time using a right to left pass of the array
Solves it is using divide and conquer in time [latex]\Theta[/latex](nlogn)
